strategy.audience: Non-technical small-business leader, AI level 0-6 of 10 (POSITIONING.md §4): an owner, operations lead or team lead in a 5-50 person company responsible for one repeated process. Specifically someone who has been told they need an agent.
strategy.concept: The same job run twice on screen - one paragraph of written instructions, then a multi-step build - with the comparison happening in the footage rather than in an argument. Then the same lesson taken from our own work: a hundred and fifteen measurements across two hundred and sixty-eight videos separated nothing, and the one instruction that survived was a question we could have asked on day one.

filter.ai_boundary: A written paragraph plus three checks keeps the judgement with the person running the task; they can read every line and change any of it. A multi-step build moves that judgement into software that has no owner in the room.
filter.friction: The advice on offer is to build a multi-step agent, and nobody in a company of nine can maintain one. The elaborate version fails quietly, at a step nobody in the room can read.
filter.next_action: Write the task out as one paragraph with three checks and run it by hand five times this week before automating anything.
filter.process: A knowledge task the team repeats about five times a week: a quote, a call summary, a reply to a standard enquiry, a weekly status note - something with a clear input, a clear output and a person who owns it.

strategy.objective: Get one viewer to write their repeated task out as a single paragraph with three checks and run it by hand five times before commissioning anything larger.
strategy.promise: A first version that works this week and that the person doing the job can change without asking anybody.
strategy.rationale: Agent building is the highest-lift topic in the corpus (n=27, median view_lift 6.63) and 23 reels carry an agent_build solution type; not one of them argues against the build (I-25). myth_bust carries the second-highest robust_z of any narrative at 1.93 on the smallest explanation share, which is this reel's shape. The register risk is real - contrarian hooks sit at 0.0076 share and 0.0139 save, the lowest of the large hook cells - so the reel opens on the demo, not on the disagreement.

title: The paragraph that beat the agents

traceability.evidence_summary: Our own elaborate version lost: 115 numeric features over 268 analysis-ready videos, none separating the strong from the weak quartile at p<0.01, only seven at p<0.05, and of 460 correlation pairs just 13 clear the reliability bar with none against reach (I-22). The single instruction that survived was 'put a real screen on camera' (I-08, rho +0.203, p=0.00085, survives creator normalisation) - a question we could have asked on day one. The angle takes the energy of the corpus's highest-lift topic and refuses its shape: agent building runs at n=27, median view_lift 6.63, and not one of the 23 agent_build reels argues against the build (I-25; the nearest counter-example, DcbPb2yxrTx, argues against the dashboard and for the architecture underneath, not against building). The visual model is the single unbroken process shot, the highest median view_lift of any visual sequence with more than three reels behind it (30.90 on n=6, 4 creators; only a three-reel sequence scores higher), carried here by DbVKVz0y8xo's 87-second unbroken take at 33.0 shares and 57.6 saves per 1 000; DVaBP3wDAFE (70.4x lift) supplies the look of the elaborate run as a foil, DZQZOVhgNvK (50.2 saves/1k) the output-before-architecture ordering, Dbs2JdJKUDd (robust_z 3.28) the pain-demo-objection order.
traceability.original_synthesis: The corpus contains 27 agent-build reels and 23 with an agent_build solution type, and not one of them argues against the build - the nearest thing to a counter-example, DcbPb2yxrTx ('Please stop building Jarvis dashboards', myth_bust / warning_dont), argues against the visible dashboard and for the architecture underneath it. A demonstrated 'the small version won', with the author's own overbuild shown as the evidence, is unrepresented. The three questions - who can change it, what happens when it is wrong, how long until the first version runs - are ours and appear in no reference.
traceability.why_better_than_generic: A generic AI script would praise agents or, in the contrarian version, call them hype and show nothing. This one opens on the demo rather than the disagreement, because contrarian hooks carry the lowest share and save rates of the large hook cells (0.0076 and 0.0139), runs both versions in the footage so the comparison is watchable rather than arguable, and uses our own failed measurement as the proof - which means the reel's evidence is a thing we did badly, not a thing we are selling.
